blocks.en: Unit 4 · Abraham — Father of Faith
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 4 · Abraham — Padre de la Fe

blocks.en: 1. The Call: Leave Everything
blocks.es_reference: 1. El Llamado: Dejarlo Todo

blocks.en: In Genesis 12, God spoke to Abram (later Abraham) with two imperatives, each carrying promises. First: "Get out of your country, from your family and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you." The corresponding promise: "I will make you a great nation." Second, and often mistranslated: "Be a blessing." Not merely "you shall be a blessing" — it is a command. You have a choice in whether you will be a blessing to others. Think of the faith this required: leave everything familiar, go to an unknown land, with only God's word as your guide. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran. Not the age of new beginnings in any culture — and yet that is exactly what God called him to.
blocks.es_reference: En Génesis 12, Dios habló a Abram (más tarde Abraham) con dos imperativos, cada uno con promesas. Primero: "Vete de tu tierra, de tu parentela y de la casa de tu padre, a la tierra que te mostraré". La promesa correspondiente: "Haré de ti una nación grande". Segundo, a menudo mal traducido: "Sé bendición" — no meramente "serás bendición", sino un mandamiento. Tú tienes la opción de ser una bendición para otros. Piensa en la fe que esto requirió: dejar todo lo familiar, ir a una tierra desconocida, solo con la palabra de Dios como guía. Abram tenía setenta y cinco años cuando partió de Harán. No es la edad de nuevos comienzos en ninguna cultura — y sin embargo, a eso exactamente lo llamó Dios.

blocks.en: Genesis 12:1-3 (NKJV): "Now the Lord had said to Abram: 'Get out of your country, from your family and from your father's house, to a land that I will show you. I will make you a great nation; I will bless you and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing. I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who curses you; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.'"
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 12:1-3 (RVG): "Pero Jehová había dicho a Abram: Vete de tu tierra y de tu parentela, y de la casa de tu padre, a la tierra que te mostraré. Y haré de ti una nación grande, y te bendeciré, y engrandeceré tu nombre, y serás bendición. Bendeciré a los que te bendijeren, y a los que te maldijeren maldeciré; y serán benditas en ti todas las familias de la tierra."

blocks.en: 2. Abram Obeyed and Worshiped
blocks.es_reference: 2. Abram Obedeció y Adoró

blocks.en: Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all their possessions — including "the people which they had acquired." The Hebrew word for "acquired" carries the meaning of proselytizing. These were people who had come to know God because of Abram. He was already being a blessing before he ever set foot in Canaan. When they reached the promised land, God appeared to Abram at Shechem and promised the land to his descendants. Abram built an altar — his first recorded act in the land was worship. Later he built another altar between Bethel and Ai and called upon the name of the Lord. The pattern is set: the man of faith establishes worship before he establishes anything else.
blocks.es_reference: Abram tomó a su esposa Sarai, a su sobrino Lot y todas sus posesiones — incluyendo "las personas que habían adquirido". La palabra hebrea para "adquirido" tiene el significado de proselitismo. Eran personas que llegaron a conocer a Dios gracias a Abram. Ya estaba siendo una bendición antes de poner un pie en Canaán. Cuando llegaron a la tierra prometida, Dios se apareció a Abram en Siquem y le prometió la tierra a sus descendientes. Abram construyó un altar — su primer acto registrado en la tierra fue adoración. Más tarde construyó otro altar entre Betel y Hai e invocó el nombre de Jehová. El patrón está establecido: el hombre de fe establece la adoración antes que cualquier otra cosa.

blocks.en: 3. A Failure of Faith in Egypt
blocks.es_reference: 3. Un Fracaso de Fe en Egipto

blocks.en: A severe famine drove Abram to Egypt. Fearing for his life because Sarai was beautiful, he asked her to say she was his sister — a half-truth, as she was indeed his half-sister, but a deception nonetheless. Abram was not trusting God's protection but his own clever devices. Pharaoh took Sarai into his house, and God struck Pharaoh with plagues. When Pharaoh discovered the truth, he sent Abram away with great wealth — sheep, oxen, donkeys, servants, and camels. God used even Abram's failure to begin fulfilling His promises. Abram was now a very wealthy man, but not because of his own cleverness. Because of God's mercy.
blocks.es_reference: Una severa hambruna llevó a Abram a Egipto. Temiendo por su vida porque Sarai era hermosa, le pidió que dijera que era su hermana — una media verdad, ya que era su media hermana, pero un engaño de todos modos. Abram no confiaba en la protección de Dios sino en sus propios artificios. Faraón tomó a Sarai en su casa, y Dios hirió a Faraón con plagas. Cuando Faraón descubrió la verdad, despidió a Abram con gran riqueza — ovejas, bueyes, asnos, siervos y camellos. Dios usó incluso el fracaso de Abram para comenzar a cumplir Sus promesas. Abram era ahora un hombre muy rico, pero no por su propia astucia. Sino por la misericordia de Dios.

blocks.en: Pastoral Note: Have you ever manipulated circumstances because you were afraid? God's mercy can redeem even our failures. But don't mistake that for permission to keep failing. Faith means trusting before the crisis, not cleaning up after.
blocks.es_reference: Nota Pastoral: ¿Alguna vez has manipulado las circunstancias por miedo? La misericordia de Dios puede redimir incluso nuestros fracasos. Pero no confundas eso con permiso para seguir fallando. La fe significa confiar antes de la crisis, no limpiar después.

blocks.en: 4. Abram Lets Lot Choose First
blocks.es_reference: 4. Abram Deja que Lot Elija Primero

blocks.en: Abram and Lot had become so wealthy that the land could not support both. Strife arose between their herdsmen. Abram, fresh from his failure in Egypt, showed remarkable growth. He gave Lot first choice: "If you take the left, I will go right; if you take the right, I will go left." Lot chose the well-watered Jordan Valley near Sodom — a choice made by sight, not by faith. Abram took the remaining land. Then God spoke again: "Lift your eyes and look... all the land you see I will give to you and your descendants forever." Abram had let go of his rights, and God gave him everything. The man who could afford to be generous because his security was in God, not in real estate.
blocks.es_reference: Abram y Lot se habían vuelto tan ricos que la tierra no podía sostener a ambos. Surgió conflicto entre sus pastores. Abram, recién salido de su fracaso en Egipto, mostró un crecimiento notable. Dio a Lot la primera opción: "Si tomas la izquierda, yo iré a la derecha; si tomas la derecha, yo iré a la izquierda". Lot eligió el valle del Jordán bien regado, cerca de Sodoma — una elección hecha por la vista, no por la fe. Abram tomó la tierra restante. Entonces Dios habló de nuevo: "Alza tus ojos y mira... toda la tierra que ves la daré a ti y a tu descendencia para siempre". Abram había renunciado a sus derechos, y Dios le dio todo. El hombre que podía permitirse ser generoso porque su seguridad estaba en Dios, no en bienes raíces.

blocks.en: 5. Rescuing Lot: Faith in Action
blocks.es_reference: 5. Rescatando a Lot: Fe en Acción

blocks.en: When Lot was taken captive by invading kings, Abram could have seen this as God removing the competition. Instead, he armed 318 trained men born in his house, pursued the enemy to Dan, divided his forces by night, and defeated four kings at once. He brought back Lot, his family, and all the possessions. This is not the cautious Abram who lied in Egypt. This is a man whose faith now acts decisively when others are in danger. Faith is not passive; it is not always patient waiting. Sometimes faith straps on a sword and rides through the night.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Lot fue tomado cautivo por reyes invasores, Abram pudo haber visto esto como Dios eliminando la competencia. En cambio, armó a 318 hombres entrenados nacidos en su casa, persiguió al enemigo hasta Dan, dividió sus fuerzas de noche y derrotó a cuatro reyes a la vez. Trajo de vuelta a Lot, su familia y todas las posesiones. Este no es el Abram cauteloso que mintió en Egipto. Este es un hombre cuya fe ahora actúa decisivamente cuando otros están en peligro. La fe no es pasiva; no es siempre espera paciente. A veces la fe se ciñe la espada y cabalga durante la noche.

blocks.en: 6. Melchizedek: King of Righteousness
blocks.es_reference: 6. Melquisedec: Rey de Justicia

blocks.en: After the battle, Melchizedek, king of Salem (Jerusalem) and priest of God Most High, brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram. The name Melchizedek means "King of Righteousness." Abram gave him a tenth of everything. Contrast this with the king of Sodom, who offered Abram all the recovered goods if he would return the people. Abram refused: "I will not take a thread or a sandal strap from you, lest you say, 'I have made Abram rich.'" Abram wanted to be indebted only to God. Melchizedek is one of Scripture's most mysterious figures — appearing without genealogy, blessing Abram, then disappearing. Hebrews 7 declares him a foreshadowing of Christ, our eternal High Priest.
blocks.es_reference: Después de la batalla, Melquisedec, rey de Salem (Jerusalén) y sacerdote del Dios Altísimo, sacó pan y vino y bendijo a Abram. El nombre Melquisedec significa "Rey de Justicia". Abram le dio los diezmos de todo. Contrasta esto con el rey de Sodoma, quien ofreció a Abram los bienes recuperados si devolvía las personas. Abram se negó: "No tomaré ni un hilo ni una correa de calzado de ti, para que no digas: Yo enriquecí a Abram". Abram quería estar en deuda solo con Dios. Melquisedec es una de las figuras más misteriosas de la Escritura — aparece sin genealogía, bendice a Abram y luego desaparece. Hebreos 7 lo declara un presagio de Cristo, nuestro eterno Sumo Sacerdote.

blocks.en: Genesis 14:18-20 (NKJV): "Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was the priest of God Most High. And he blessed him and said: 'Blessed be Abram of God Most High, Possessor of heaven and earth; and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.' And he gave him a tithe of all."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 14:18-20 (RVG): "Entonces Melquisedec, rey de Salem, sacó pan y vino; él era sacerdote del Dios Altísimo, y le bendijo, diciendo: Bendito sea Abram del Dios Altísimo, creador de los cielos y de la tierra; y bendito sea el Dios Altísimo, que entregó tus enemigos en tu mano. Y le dio Abram los diezmos de todo."

blocks.en: 7. The Covenant: Faith Credited as Righteousness
blocks.es_reference: 7. El Pacto: Fe Contada por Justicia

blocks.en: Abram lamented that he remained childless; his heir was Eliezer of Damascus. God took him outside and said, "Count the stars, if you are able to count them. So shall your descendants be." Then comes one of the most important verses in the Old Testament:
blocks.es_reference: Abram lamentó que seguía sin hijos; su heredero era Eliezer de Damasco. Dios lo llevó afuera y le dijo: "Mira ahora los cielos y cuenta las estrellas, si las puedes contar. Así será tu descendencia". Entonces viene uno de los versículos más importantes del Antiguo Testamento:

blocks.en: Genesis 15:6 (NKJV): "And he believed in the Lord, and He accounted it to him for righteousness."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 15:6 (RVG): "Y creyó a Jehová, y le fue contado por justicia."

blocks.en: No deep theological understanding. No works. No circumcision yet. Simply belief. Paul would later build the doctrine of justification by faith on this verse (Romans 4). God then formalized the covenant with a ritual — animals cut in two, a smoking oven and flaming torch passing between them. Only God passed through, signifying that this covenant was unconditional. He alone bound Himself to keep it. He also revealed that Abram's descendants would be enslaved for 400 years, but would come out with great possessions — a prophecy fulfilled in the Exodus.
blocks.es_reference: Ninguna comprensión teológica profunda. Ninguna obra. Aún sin circuncisión. Simplemente creer. Pablo más tarde construiría la doctrina de la justificación por la fe sobre este versículo (Romanos 4). Luego Dios formalizó el pacto con un ritual — animales partidos por la mitad, un horno humeante y una antorcha de fuego pasando entre las piezas. Solo Dios pasó, significando que este pacto era incondicional. Él solo se obligó a guardarlo. También reveló que los descendientes de Abram serían esclavizados por 400 años, pero saldrían con grandes posesiones — una profecía cumplida en el Éxodo.

blocks.en: 8. Hagar and Ishmael: Taking Matters into Our Own Hands
blocks.es_reference: 8. Agar e Ismael: Tomando Cartas en el Asunto

blocks.en: Ten years after arriving in Canaan, Sarai still had no child. She gave her Egyptian maidservant Hagar to Abram as a wife. Hagar conceived and despised Sarai. Sarai mistreated her, and Hagar fled. The angel of the Lord found her by a spring and said, "Return and submit." Then he promised: "I will multiply your descendants exceedingly." Hagar named the Lord "You are the God who sees me" (El Roi). She bore Ishmael, but this was not God's plan. Abram was eighty-six years old. Faith often involves waiting — and we so often fail that test. The consequences of Ishmael's birth ripple forward into the geopolitics of the Middle East to this very day.
blocks.es_reference: Diez años después de llegar a Canaán, Sarai aún no tenía hijos. Dio a su sierva egipcia Agar a Abram como esposa. Agar concibió y menospreció a Sarai. Sarai la maltrató, y Agar huyó. El ángel de Jehová la encontró junto a un manantial y dijo: "Vuelve y sométete". Luego prometió: "Multiplicaré tanto tu descendencia que no se podrá contar". Agar llamó al Señor "Tú eres el Dios que me ve" (El Roi). Dio a luz a Ismael, pero este no era el plan de Dios. Abram tenía ochenta y seis años. La fe a menudo implica esperar — y nosotros fallamos esa prueba con tanta frecuencia. Las consecuencias del nacimiento de Ismael repercuten hasta hoy en la geopolítica del Medio Oriente.

blocks.en: 9. Name Changes and the Covenant of Circumcision
blocks.es_reference: 9. Cambios de Nombre y el Pacto de la Circuncisión

blocks.en: When Abram was ninety-nine — thirteen years after Ishmael — God appeared again. "I am Almighty God (El Shaddai); walk before Me and be blameless." He changed Abram's name ("exalted father") to Abraham ("father of a multitude"). Sarai ("my princess") became Sarah ("princess" — no longer just "my," but for all nations). God instituted circumcision as the sign of the covenant. Abraham laughed at the thought that a hundred-year-old man and ninety-year-old woman could have a child, but God said, "Sarah shall bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac" (meaning "he laughs"). God also blessed Ishmael — but the covenant would be established through Isaac.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Abram tenía noventa y nueve años — trece años después de Ismael — Dios se apareció de nuevo. "Yo soy el Dios Todopoderoso (El Shaddai); anda delante de mí y sé perfecto". Cambió el nombre de Abram ("padre exaltado") a Abraham ("padre de multitudes"). Sarai ("mi princesa") se convirtió en Sara ("princesa" — ya no solo "mía" sino para todas las naciones). Dios instituyó la circuncisión como la señal del pacto. Abraham se rió pensando que un hombre de cien años y una mujer de noventa podrían tener un hijo, pero Dios dijo: "Sara te dará a luz un hijo, y llamarás su nombre Isaac" (que significa "él se ríe"). Dios también bendijo a Ismael — pero el pacto se establecería a través de Isaac.

blocks.en: 10. The Offering of Isaac: The Ultimate Test
blocks.es_reference: 10. La Ofrenda de Isaac: La Prueba Suprema

blocks.en: Then God tested Abraham. "Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and offer him as a burnt offering." No hesitation. Early the next morning, Abraham set out. For three days he walked, telling his servants, "We will worship and return to you." He believed God would raise Isaac from the dead (Hebrews 11:19) — there is no other way to read his words. Isaac asked, "Where is the lamb?" Abraham replied, "God will provide for Himself the lamb." At the moment Abraham raised the knife, the angel stopped him. A ram caught in the thicket became the substitute. Abraham named the place "The Lord Will Provide" (Jehovah Jireh). Two thousand years later, on that same mountain range, the Lamb of God would be offered — but no angel would stop the knife. The substitute Abraham received pointed forward to the Substitute we received.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Dios probó a Abraham. "Toma ahora tu hijo, tu único hijo Isaac, a quien amas, y ofrécelo en holocausto". Sin vacilación. Temprano a la mañana siguiente, Abraham partió. Durante tres días caminó, diciendo a sus siervos: "Adoraremos y volveremos a vosotros". Creía que Dios resucitaría a Isaac de los muertos (Hebreos 11:19) — no hay otra forma de leer sus palabras. Isaac preguntó: "¿Dónde está el cordero?" Abraham respondió: "Dios proveerá para sí el cordero". En el momento en que Abraham alzó el cuchillo, el ángel lo detuvo. Un carnero enredado en un zarzal se convirtió en el sustituto. Abraham llamó al lugar "Jehová Proveerá" (Jehová Jireh). Dos mil años después, en esa misma cadena montañosa, el Cordero de Dios sería ofrecido — pero ningún ángel detendría el cuchillo. El sustituto que recibió Abraham apuntaba hacia el Sustituto que nosotros recibimos.

blocks.en: Application: What is your Isaac? The thing you love most that God is asking you to surrender? The lesson is not that God always stops the knife — sometimes He doesn't. The lesson is that God provides, and He is worth trusting even when you don't understand.
blocks.es_reference: Aplicación: ¿Cuál es tu Isaac? ¿Lo que más amas que Dios te pide que entregues? La lección no es que Dios siempre detiene el cuchillo — a veces no lo hace. La lección es que Dios provee, y vale la pena confiar en Él incluso cuando no entiendes.

blocks.en: 11. The Pattern: Seldom Early, Never Late
blocks.es_reference: 11. El Patrón: Rara vez Temprano, Nunca Tarde

blocks.en: Abraham waited twenty-five years from the promise to Isaac's birth. He failed, doubted, and manipulated. But God never abandoned him. The pattern of God's work in Abraham — and in your life and ministry — is this: God is seldom early, never late, and always on time. He makes promises. We try to help. He waits. We panic. He provides. Trust the pattern. The ram in the thicket arrived just in time, not before — never before. That is how He works. And He has not changed.
blocks.es_reference: Abraham esperó veinticinco años desde la promesa hasta el nacimiento de Isaac. Falló, dudó y manipuló. Pero Dios nunca lo abandonó. El patrón del obrar de Dios en Abraham — y en tu vida y ministerio — es este: Dios rara vez es temprano, nunca es tarde, y siempre a tiempo. Él hace promesas. Nosotros tratamos de ayudar. Él espera. Nosotros entramos en pánico. Él provee. Confía en el patrón. El carnero en el zarzal llegó justo a tiempo, no antes — nunca antes. Así es como Él obra. Y no ha cambiado.

mc.stem: How old was Abram when he departed from Haran to go to Canaan?
mc.why: Correct. Abram was 75 years old — not the age of new beginnings in any culture, but exactly what God called him to.

mc.stem: The second imperative God gave Abram is better translated as what?
mc.why: Yes. 'Be a blessing' is a command, not just a promise — Abram had a choice in the matter.

mc.stem: What does the Hebrew word for 'acquired' (the people they had in Haran) imply?
options: They proselytized — people came to God through Abram
mc.why: Correct. Abram was already being a blessing by leading others to God before he ever set foot in Canaan.

mc.stem: What did Abram do first when he arrived in Canaan?
options: Built an altar and called on God
mc.why: Yes. Abram's first act in the promised land was worship. The man of faith establishes worship before anything else.

mc.stem: Why did Abram go to Egypt during the famine?
mc.why: Correct. The famine was severe, so Abram went to Egypt for provision. The text gives no indication this was God's command.

mc.stem: What half-truth did Abram tell about Sarai in Egypt?
mc.why: Correct. Sarai was his half-sister, so it was a half-truth — but still deception in intent.

mc.stem: How did God protect Sarai in Pharaoh's house?
mc.why: Yes. God struck Pharaoh's house with plagues until he discovered the truth and released Sarai.

mc.stem: When strife arose between Abram's and Lot's herdsmen, what did Abram do?
options: Gave Lot first choice of the land
mc.why: Correct. Abram let Lot choose first — remarkable humility and faith. Abram's security was in God, not in real estate.

mc.stem: Where did Lot choose to settle?
options: The well-watered Jordan Valley near Sodom
mc.why: Yes. Lot chose by sight, not faith — the well-watered plain near wicked Sodom. The choice would cost him dearly.

mc.stem: After Abram let Lot choose first, what did God promise him?
options: 'All the land you see I will give to you and your descendants'
mc.why: Correct. When Abram released his rights, God gave him everything in sight.

mc.stem: Who was Melchizedek?
options: King of Salem and priest of God Most High
mc.why: Yes. Melchizedek means 'King of Righteousness' — a foreshadowing of Christ, our eternal High Priest (Hebrews 7).

mc.stem: What did Abram give Melchizedek?
mc.why: Correct. Abram tithed to Melchizedek, recognizing his spiritual authority before any Levitical priesthood existed.

mc.stem: Why did Abram refuse the king of Sodom's offer of goods?
options: He didn't want the king to claim 'I made Abram rich'
mc.why: Exactly. Abram wanted to be indebted only to God — his blessing must come from heaven, not from Sodom.

mc.stem: What did Abram lament before God in Genesis 15?
options: His childlessness — his heir was Eliezer
mc.why: Yes. Abram was childless and his heir was a servant from Damascus. God's response: count the stars.

mc.stem: What does Genesis 15:6 say about Abram's faith?
options: 'He believed in the Lord, and it was accounted to him for righteousness'
mc.why: Yes! This is the cornerstone verse for justification by faith — Paul builds Romans 4 on this single verse.

mc.stem: Who was Hagar?
mc.why: Correct. Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian servant, given to Abram in an attempt to fulfill God's promise their own way.

mc.stem: What did Hagar name God when He met her in the wilderness?
options: El Roi — 'You are the God who sees me'
mc.why: Yes. El Roi — God sees the afflicted and the outcast. The first person in Scripture to name God is a foreign maidservant.

mc.stem: What does the name 'Isaac' mean?
mc.why: Yes. Isaac means 'he laughs' — Abraham laughed in disbelief, Sarah laughed in surprise, and God had the last laugh.

mc.stem: How did Abraham respond when God told him to offer Isaac as a burnt offering?
options: He set out early the next morning
mc.why: Correct. No hesitation — Abraham trusted God would provide or raise Isaac from the dead (Hebrews 11:19).

mc.stem: What did Abraham name the place where God provided the ram?
mc.why: Yes. Jehovah Jireh — a name that echoes through every generation. On that same mountain range, the Lamb of God was later offered.

sa.prompt: Explain the two imperatives God gave Abram in Genesis 12:1-3 and what they teach about faith.
sa.model: God commanded Abram to leave everything familiar AND to actively be a blessing. Faith requires both leaving and giving.

sa.prompt: How did Abram fail in Egypt, and how did God show mercy despite that failure?
sa.model: Abram lied about Sarai out of fear. God struck Pharaoh with plagues, and Abram left wealthy — mercy redeeming failure.

sa.prompt: What does Abram's willingness to let Lot choose first reveal about his character growth?
sa.model: Abram had grown from manipulating in Egypt to trusting God, releasing his rights, and avoiding strife.

sa.prompt: Who was Melchizedek, and why is he significant for understanding Christ?
sa.model: Melchizedek was both king and priest, foreshadowing Christ as our eternal High Priest (Hebrews 7).

sa.prompt: Why is Genesis 15:6 a foundational verse for the doctrine of justification by faith?
sa.model: Abram was declared righteous simply by believing God's promise — before circumcision, before works. Paul builds Romans 4 on it.

sa.prompt: What went wrong when Abram and Sarai tried to fulfill God's promise through Hagar?
sa.model: They took matters into their own hands instead of waiting on God's timing, causing family conflict and lasting consequences.

sa.prompt: What do the name changes from Abram to Abraham and Sarai to Sarah signify?
sa.model: Abram became 'father of a multitude'; Sarai became 'princess' for all nations — no longer just 'my' princess.

sa.prompt: What did Abraham believe about God's ability to keep His promise when he went to offer Isaac?
sa.model: Abraham believed God could raise Isaac from the dead (Hebrews 11:19). He trusted the promise completely.

sa.prompt: What does 'Jehovah Jireh' mean, and what does it teach about God's character?
sa.model: It means 'The Lord Will Provide' — God sees our need and provides the substitute, ultimately Christ.

sa.prompt: Explain the pattern: 'God is seldom early, never late, and always on time.' How did this play out in Abraham's life?
sa.model: Abraham waited 25 years from promise to Isaac's birth. He tried to help (Ishmael), but God's timing was perfect.
